findings.title: When the rule editor's save is refused 422 automation_rule.restricted_token_stale (a token pasted from another version or rule, the F-DG6-640 path, or a pre-0127 token), the editor suppresses the corrected problem text and tells the author in EN and AR 'This rule changed after you opened it … re-apply your change', which is untrue (the If-Match matched, the rule did not change); re-applying the same change gives the same false message again
findings.reproduction: Candidate c45d73b8 (source 33db1a46). Production-initialized stack (apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh), chromium-en and chromium-ar; probe docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/domain/round-11/probes/dom-r11-editor-tokens.spec.ts.txt part C, log probe-editor-tokens.log. A synthetic ADM_METHOD author, not admitted to sensitive records, publishes rule version 1 = [benefitId neq P, neq S, neq H] (S and H marked sensitive by the TO) through the real dry run, submit, TO review and publish. In draft version 2 the author clicks 'Remove condition 2' (S) and saves three times (row version 4). To restore 'exclude S' the author copies the token shown for S on the published version 1 page ('[restricted:<24 hex>:2]'), clicks 'Add a condition', enters benefitId / does not equal / the token, and clicks 'Save the draft'. Then the author does what the alert says: re-applies the same change and saves again.
findings.expected: The integrity behaviour is correct and must stay: the PATCH is refused 422 restricted_token_stale and nothing is stored (F-DG6-640 is fixed). What the author is told must be true for the release it ships in, in EN and AR (the F-DG4-160 standard; CLAUDE.md honesty rules). D-233 / T-DG6-BE-Z15 corrected the problem text for exactly this case ('… not issued for this version as it now stands (it comes from an earlier save, another version or another rule): reload the version and re-apply your change'), but the editor never shows it. For a 422 stale (If-Match matched), the editor should say that a restricted value was not issued for this version (for example, that a restricted value copied from another version or rule cannot be reused here, and that only someone admitted to the record can add it), not that the rule changed. A 409 can keep the current 'changed' alert.
findings.actual: PATCH If-Match 4 -> 422 automation_rule.restricted_token_stale with the corrected detail (log: 'C last PATCH status=422 problem=…'). Draft v2 stays [P, H] at row version 4, so the rule did not change. RulePage.tsx EditContent maps 409 and 422-stale alike through isChangedSinceRead: runner.clear() drops the problem text, and the form shows only workflowsP5.rules.changedReapply: 'This rule changed after you opened it. The form now shows the current version: re-apply your change, then save the draft again.' / 'تغيّرت هذه القاعدة بعد أن فتحتها. يعرض النموذج الآن الإصدار الحالي: أعد تطبيق تعديلك، ثم احفظ المسودة مرة أخرى.' (screens/en/dom-r11-C4-after-save.png, screens/ar/dom-r11-C4-after-save.png). Following the instruction (re-apply, save) gives the same 422 and the same alert again (…-C5-reapply-after-save.png). The editor reloads after every successful save, so a 422 stale is reached from the UI only by a pasted foreign token or by a token issued before migration 0127. In both cases the rule has not changed, so the alert is false in every UI case where a 422 triggers it. ADR-0051 amendment part B and the BE-Z15 handback (item 2; 'the real-browser flow was not re-run with a pasted token') document the alert; neither notices that it is untrue for the new cases. Bounded: no stored value changes, no hidden literal is disclosed or misplaced, no business approval is affected. Low, by the F-DG4-160 precedent (untrue user-facing text, EN and AR). Suggested repair: in EditContent, show changedReapply for a 409 only; for a 422 stale, reload too but show a separate en/ar message (or the problem text) that explains that the restricted value cannot be used in this version. Pin both in rule-editor-tokens-z14.test.tsx.

history.note: Raised in DG6 round 11 by domain-reviewer. The assignment asks reviewers to challenge D-226 to D-234 for 'a misleading screen'. F-DG6-640 itself is CLOSED_VERIFIED in this round: the token is refused and nothing is stored. This finding covers only what the author is told on that refusal. Low and non-blocking (F-DG4-160 precedent). It is not accepted as an observation by the reporter, because the fix is small and the text is untrue in EN and AR.
